FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 11 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 July 1989, after the draft finalized by the Physical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard was first published in 1971 and has been basis of experience gained during its use. revised for incorporating changes on the

In the preparation of this standard, due weightage has been given to the testing practices followed in the country in this field. This standard forms a part of series of standards under the title cords and tyre cord warpsheets made from man-made fibres'. `Methods of test for tyre yarns, container in the

The methods prescribed in the standard presume that the mass of each individual lot would be specified by the seller in the invoice note.

In reporting the results of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

SSECLAL METHOD OF DETERMINING THE COM.MERCIAL MASS OF LARGE PACKAGES A-l PRINCIPLE A-l.1 This method is based on the measurement of total length of yarn on the package and on the determination of oven-dry mass of the yarn per unit length. A-lJ.1 Under well definedconditions, the ovendry mass of the whole package can be deduced. A-2, APPARATUS A-2.1 The apparatus shall consist of a winding frame fitted with a device enabling the length of yarn wodnd-on to be measured to within about one percent. *A-2.2 Winding Frame The winding frame shall have a speed not greater than 200 mimia The unwinding tension shall be maintained in the range of 5 f 1 mN/tex. 2 A-2.3 Length Measuring Device This device consists of a measuring roller A of uniform diameter `( not less than 100 mm of hard, smooth material ) on the shaft of which is mounted a revolution counter as shown in Fig. 1. A roller of soft material B presse$ against the measuring roller. The load applied to the pressure roller shall not be, less than 100 g/cm of the line of contact between the two rollers. Check the surface of the measuring roller at frequent intervals to ensure that it is in good condition. A-2.3.1 Check to ensure page: that there is no siip-

a) by testing theaccuiacy.of the readings given by the revolution counter `after repeated winding of the same piece of yarn. Some discrepancies may arise from the possible .crushing of the yarn. between the rollers or from change in twist duiing repeated
